steps: Given: T_c = 30°C
Required: Temperature on Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales (T_f and T_k)
Formula: T_f = (9/5) × T_c + 32°
Substitution: T_f = (9/5) × 30°C + 32°
Working: T_f = 54° + 32° = 86°F
Formula: T_k = T_c + 273
Substitution: T_k = 30°C + 273
Working: T_k = 303 K
Result: T_f = 86°F and T_k = 303 K
The molecules of a solid are closely packed and have strong forces of attraction between them.
They vibrate about their fixed positions and cannot move freely from place to place.
Therefore, a solid has a fixed shape and a fixed volume.
items.finalAnswer: Closely packed molecules vibrate about fixed positions, so a solid has a fixed shape and volume.

steps: The molecules of a gas are far apart and the forces of attraction between them are very weak.
They move freely and randomly in all directions.
Therefore, gas molecules spread out to fill their container and gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume.
items.finalAnswer: Gas molecules move freely and spread out to fill their container, so a gas has neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume.

steps: In a solid, molecules are very closely packed together.
In a liquid, molecules are less closely packed than in a solid, but remain close to one another.
In a gas, molecules are very far apart.
items.finalAnswer: Molecules are closest in solids, farther apart in liquids, and very far apart in gases.

steps: When the temperature of a liquid is raised, its molecules gain kinetic energy and move faster.
The increased motion causes the liquid to expand.
items.finalAnswer: Raising a liquid’s temperature makes its molecules move faster and causes the liquid to expand.

steps: The temperature of a body is the measure of its degree of hotness or coldness.
items.finalAnswer: Temperature is the measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

steps: Heat is energy in transit from a body at a higher temperature to a body at a lower temperature because of the temperature difference between them.
items.finalAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body due to a temperature difference.

steps: A thermometric property is a property of a substance that changes with temperature and can be used to measure temperature.
Examples include the volume of a liquid, the pressure of a gas at constant volume, the electrical resistance of a conductor, and the electromotive force of a thermocouple.
items.finalAnswer: A thermometric property changes with temperature and is used to measure it; examples include liquid volume, gas pressure, electrical resistance, and thermocouple emf.
